purpose: Source-ground professional methodology rules for training, evaluation, and release decisions without bundling copyrighted full text.

normative_requirement.definition: A requirement stated by the selected current conduct, reporting, appraisal, certainty, governance, or protocol authority within its declared scope.

primary_study_empirical.definition: A measured result from a named primary methods study; it remains population, task, model, and version specific.

project_calibrated.definition: A decision threshold estimated on a frozen project development set and evaluated once on dependency-isolated held-out families.

engineering_placeholder.definition: A provisional implementation value used only to exercise software before calibration.

distribution_policy.rule: The public skill carries identities, source URLs, hashes, scope notes, and rule anchors only. Full text remains in a Git-ignored lawful cache and must be reacquired under the source license or access terms.

sources.title: Cochrane Handbook Chapter 1: Starting a review
sources.read_scope: Key points; question relevance; team roles; advance protocol decisions; question-method direction; decision records.

local_artifacts.access_route: official Cochrane HTML converted to text

supported_rules.statement: The review question determines the methods; available tools or methods must not determine the question.
Question formulation must address an important user decision and include relevant perspectives.
Methods and material judgments should be established in advance and not depend on included-study findings.

unsupported_inferences: This intervention-review chapter does not define universal rules for every review family.
It does not validate an AI model or numeric automation threshold.

sources.title: Cochrane Handbook Chapter 2: Determining the scope of the review and the questions it will address
sources.read_scope: Key points; FINER and scoping; existing-review checks; broad versus narrow scope; stakeholder and decision relevance.

local_artifacts.access_route: official Cochrane HTML converted to text

supported_rules.statement: Scope should be chosen for decision relevance, answerability, and feasibility after structured scoping rather than novelty alone.
Before starting, check existing reviews and registrations and classify whether a new review, update, or other response is justified.
Review breadth and statistical pooling are separate decisions; broad scope can aid decisions while an over-broad pooled effect can become uninterpretable.

unsupported_inferences: FINER is not a validated model score or automatic go/no-go threshold.
A broad review is not automatically a network meta-analysis.

sources.title: Cochrane Handbook Chapter 3: Defining criteria and grouping studies for synthesis
sources.read_scope: Eligibility, review PICO versus synthesis PICO versus study PICO, grouping, outcome hierarchy, and protocol independence.

local_artifacts.access_route: official Cochrane HTML converted to text

supported_rules.statement: The review PICO, each synthesis PICO, and each included-study PICO must remain distinct and linked.
Eligibility and synthesis grouping should be planned together and grouping changes must be documented without outcome-driven selection.

unsupported_inferences: The chapter does not justify arbitrary sample-size, heterogeneity, or quality cutoffs.
Study inclusion does not imply inclusion of every result in one synthesis.

sources.title: Cochrane Handbook Chapter 4: Searching for and selecting studies
sources.read_scope: Key points; source coverage; sensitivity; peer review; study-report identity; lawful access and documentation.

local_artifacts.access_route: official Cochrane HTML converted to text

supported_rules.statement: Searches should be reproducible, cover multiple relevant sources, and favor sensitivity within declared resource limits.
Studies are the primary review unit, while multiple reports and records must be linked without duplicate counting.
Database terms, licensing agreements, and copyright law govern record and publication retrieval.

unsupported_inferences: A single literature QA or RAG query is not a comprehensive systematic search.
Two independent identical searches are not required; search-strategy peer review is the relevant control.

sources.title: Cochrane Handbook Chapter 9: Summarizing study characteristics and preparing for synthesis
sources.read_scope: Synthesis PICO, pre-specified grouping, study-characteristic comparison, and preparation for synthesis.

local_artifacts.access_route: official Cochrane HTML converted to text

supported_rules.statement: Each synthesis PICO defines the question, comparison, grouping, and outcome or population subgroups for that synthesis.
Map included-study characteristics to pre-specified synthesis groups and compare them before choosing statistical synthesis.

unsupported_inferences: Terminology similarity alone does not establish clinical poolability.
A model-generated cluster cannot silently replace the protocol grouping.

sources.title: Cochrane Handbook Chapter 10: Analysing data and undertaking meta-analyses
sources.read_scope: Meta-analysis assumptions, poolability, heterogeneity, model interpretation, prediction intervals, subgroup and sensitivity analysis.

local_artifacts.access_route: official Cochrane HTML converted to text

supported_rules.statement: Meta-analysis is considered only when the synthesis studies are sufficiently similar to answer a clinically meaningful common question.
Heterogeneity must be interpreted with clinical and methodological context; simple I-squared thresholds must not act as automatic pooling gates.
Sensitivity analyses test whether conclusions depend on influential arbitrary, uncertain, or borderline decisions.

unsupported_inferences: REML, HKSJ, fixed effect, random effects, or a prediction interval is not universally correct without the case assumptions.
Statistical significance alone does not establish subgroup differences or clinical importance.

sources.title: Methodological Expectations of Cochrane Intervention Reviews
sources.read_scope: Mandatory standards C39 and C46 plus duplicate risk-of-bias and certainty passages.

local_artifacts.access_route: official Cochrane PDF converted to text

supported_rules.statement: At least two people independently determine final study inclusion, with a predefined process for disagreements.
At least two people independently extract outcome data under the intervention-review assurance standard.

unsupported_inferences: An LLM is not silently counted as an independent person.
These intervention-review mandates must not be generalized unchanged to every review family.

sources.title: JBI Manual for Evidence Synthesis
sources.read_scope: Root manual identity, review-family routing, online-versus-PDF currency warning, and permissions boundary.

local_artifacts.access_route: official JBI live manual page converted to text

supported_rules.statement: Select the methodology chapter for the evidence type and clinical or policy question; do not force intervention methods onto all review families.

unsupported_inferences: The periodically updated PDF is not automatically the latest online manual.
The manual cannot be redistributed in the public skill without permission.

sources.title: PRISMA 2020 statement and explanation and elaboration
sources.read_scope: Statement, checklist scope, explanation and elaboration, reporting-versus-conduct boundary, reproducibility and updating.

local_artifacts.access_route: Europe PMC legal fullTextXML service
Europe PMC legal fullTextXML service

supported_rules.statement: PRISMA governs transparent and complete reporting; checklist completion alone does not establish valid conduct or low bias.
Report methods and results in enough detail for readers to assess trustworthiness and for others to replicate or update the review.

unsupported_inferences: PRISMA compliance is not a risk-of-bias or certainty rating.
PRISMA does not require meta-analysis or a directional falsifiable hypothesis.

sources.title: PRISMA-P 2015 statement
sources.read_scope: Protocol reporting items, rationale, eligibility, information sources, synthesis, amendments, and registration.

local_artifacts.access_route: official open-access PDF converted to text

supported_rules.statement: The protocol records rationale, eligibility, sources, outcomes, synthesis plans, amendments, and registration before result-driven execution.

unsupported_inferences: PRISMA-P is a protocol reporting guideline, not a substitute for profile-specific conduct guidance.
Registration is not peer review or endorsement.

sources.title: PRISMA-S: reporting literature searches in systematic reviews
sources.read_scope: Information sources, complete strategy, dates, deduplication, peer review, updates, and limits.

local_artifacts.access_route: official open-access PDF converted to text

supported_rules.statement: Report each information source, complete reproducible strategies, dates, limits, deduplication, and search updating.

unsupported_inferences: Complete reporting does not prove that source selection or recall was adequate.
PRISMA-S does not replace PRESS or known-item testing.

sources.title: PRISMA-LSR extension for living systematic reviews
sources.read_scope: Living-review status, surveillance, update methods, version changes, flow diagram, and use with PRISMA 2020.

local_artifacts.access_route: Europe PMC legal fullTextXML service

supported_rules.statement: A living review reports its current status, surveillance and update methods, flow, and changes in addition to PRISMA 2020.

unsupported_inferences: PRISMA-LSR does not itself define when a review should become or cease to be living.
A periodic search without state and version lineage is not sufficient living-review evidence.

sources.title: Synthesis without meta-analysis in systematic reviews: SWiM reporting guideline
sources.read_scope: Nine reporting items, grouping, standardized metrics, synthesis methods, presentation, limitations, and vote-counting cautions.

local_artifacts.access_route: Europe PMC legal fullTextXML service

supported_rules.statement: When meta-analysis is not appropriate, report grouping, metric, synthesis method, presentation, findings, and limitations explicitly.

unsupported_inferences: SWiM is not permission for informal vote counting by statistical significance.
It is a reporting guideline rather than a universal conduct algorithm.

sources.title: AMSTAR 2: critical appraisal tool for systematic reviews
sources.read_scope: Critical domains, item ratings, overall confidence, profile boundary, and validation limitations.

local_artifacts.access_route: Europe PMC legal fullTextXML service

supported_rules.statement: Do not sum AMSTAR 2 items into an overall numeric quality score; inspect predeclared critical-domain weaknesses.

unsupported_inferences: AMSTAR 2 is not interchangeable with ROBIS or primary-study risk-of-bias tools.
The authors explicitly did not perform extensive validation of the revised tool.

sources.title: ROBINS-I: risk of bias in non-randomised studies of interventions

identity.version_or_date: published 2016; exact tool version must be pinned

sources.read_scope: Target-trial framing, seven domains, signalling questions, result-level judgments, and applicability boundary.

local_artifacts.access_route: Europe PMC legal fullTextXML service

supported_rules.statement: Assess each eligible non-randomized intervention result against an explicit target trial across the named bias domains.

unsupported_inferences: ROBINS-I is not a generic study quality score.
A draft later version cannot silently replace the pinned tool.

sources.title: PROBAST+AI: quality, risk of bias, and applicability for prediction models
sources.read_scope: Separate development and evaluation parts, domains, quality, risk of bias, applicability, and fairness context.

local_artifacts.access_route: Europe PMC legal fullTextXML service

supported_rules.statement: Prediction-model development quality and model-evaluation risk of bias are distinct assessments with profile-specific signalling questions.

unsupported_inferences: PROBAST+AI does not validate MetaWingman or a general-purpose LLM.
A development appraisal cannot stand in for external performance evaluation.

sources.title: GRADE Book live guidance snapshot

identity.version_or_date: live API snapshot retrieved 2026-08-20; each guideline object retains version and lastModified

sources.read_scope: Index identity plus final guidance on questions, outcomes, decision thresholds, intervention certainty, imprecision, and inconsistency.

local_artifacts.access_route: official GRADE Book API
official GRADE Book API guideline object
official GRADE Book API guideline object

supported_rules.statement: Certainty is judged for a defined outcome and body of evidence, not assigned as a hidden study or review score.
Prioritize outcomes important to affected people and decisions, including desirable and undesirable effects, with explicit importance ratings.
Use pre-established outcome-specific decision thresholds or ranges for interpretation and imprecision; the null is not an automatic universal threshold.

unsupported_inferences: A model may not invent minimally important differences or certainty downgrades.
The live GRADE Book changes over time, so root labels without object versions and lastModified dates are insufficient.

sources.title: Position statement on the use of AI in evidence synthesis
sources.read_scope: Joint organizational principles, accountability, oversight, reporting, developer transparency, task-specific evaluation, limitations, and protocol justification.

local_artifacts.access_route: publisher open-access article

supported_rules.statement: Evidence synthesists retain responsibility for AI use, legal and ethical compliance, and human oversight.
AI that makes or suggests judgments must be transparently reported and justified using relevant public testing, training, validation, limitations, and bias information.

unsupported_inferences: Human oversight does not mean humans must manually repeat every low-risk AI action.
The statement does not establish equivalence for any named model or task.

sources.title: RoB 2: revised tool for assessing risk of bias in randomized trials

identity.version_or_date: official current tool release dated 22 August 2019; page verified 2026-08-20

sources.read_scope: Official identity and current-version page only; local guidance download timed out and no full-text-derived rule was admitted in this registry.
unsupported_inferences: No RoB 2 signalling rule or automation threshold is admitted until the exact official guidance is acquired and read.
The official page identity alone is not enough to train or validate an appraisal model.
